_doc: Claim ledger for the held NFTT draft 'The Lagging Indicator'. Hand-written fields: id, section, text, type, and for repo-backed claims: file, find (git pickaxe string; empty = the commit that added the file), excerpt_grep, selftest, asset, liability. scripts/nftt_claim_atoms.py fills 'atom', 'excerpt' and 'selftest_result' into lagging-indicator.atoms.json. Types: sourced (backed by the repo), inference (argument, no source can force it), unproven (marked unproven in the text), steelman (the opposing case, argued fairly).

claims.text: Treating a lagging indicator as a leading one means steering by the wake.
A timed hand-coding round measures past practice, faithfully.
Reading and judging code is a real signal; someone has to know whether the agent's lines are right.
A few thousand commits of building this way.
claims.asset: The count comes from git, so anyone with the repo gets the same number.
claims.liability: Commit count measures activity, not quality; the post must not lean on it as proof of skill.

claims.text: Merges go through a script that pins the exact commit being merged and refuses if any check is pending or failing.
claims.asset: Invariant: the commit merged is the commit reviewed; a moved head or a non-SUCCESS check refuses the merge.
claims.liability: It trusts the checks it waits on; with CI switched off for budget, 'every check SUCCESS' can mean very few checks ran.

atom.subject: feat(scripts): safe_merge.sh pins head, waits for all-SUCCESS checks, refuses conflicts [NCI:64]

claims.text: It has refused me twice when a branch moved under me.
claims.evidence: CLAUDE.md handoff v3.141.0: 'it refused twice on moved heads, as designed'
claims.asset: The refusals are recorded in the handoff, written the same day.
claims.liability: The handoff is the only record; the refusals are not in a receipt, so this is the weakest sourced claim.

claims.text: Pre-commit gates block a model name typed by hand.
claims.asset: Invariant: model ids live in one registry; a hardcoded id cannot be committed.
claims.liability: A pattern gate: a new model naming scheme it does not know slips through until the pattern is updated.

claims.text: Pre-commit gates block a file moved while something still points to the old path.
claims.asset: Invariant: no live file cites a path that a commit renames or deletes.
claims.liability: By its own docstring: 'Not caught: a directory cited without a file name, and a bare basename.' A path built at runtime is invisible too.

claims.text: Pre-commit gates block a page whose text wraps badly at some screen width.
claims.asset: Invariant: one body measure per page; a container/measure mismatch fails the commit.
claims.liability: Static CSS reading: a layout bug that only appears in a real browser at an odd width still needs the screenshot sweep.

claims.text: Every merge ends with a decision receipt, and the ledger refuses edits; a correction is a new row.
claims.asset: Invariant: a filed receipt cannot be rewritten after the outcome is known, which is what makes it a leading indicator.
claims.liability: Applied per the proof file in 2ebb2b30; the live trigger was not re-queried for this plate. 'Every merge' is the rule, and coverage is about 75%, not 100%.
